assessment.walker: Ownership variable transfers to child before predecessor close. If predecessor close fails, its number is not retried; still-owned child/current handle is attempted once. If rollback also fails, primary exception identity is preserved and no descriptor returns. Original path grammar and flags retained.
assessment.constructor: Tracking/private fields initialized before wrapped metadata/query setup. Every registered descriptor is drained after constructor failure, including one whose post-acquisition validation failed. Original constructor exception identity is retained and re-raised without conversion even after cleanup failure.
assessment.registration: retain reserves None slot before acquisition; failed reservation invokes no open, failed open leaves a consumable empty slot, returned handle replaces existing slot before validation. Ordinary trusted list/single-threaded behavior assumed; no arbitrary mutation/interruption safety claim.
assessment.close: Pop before each close prevents retry of consumed numeric FDs. All registered handles attempted despite failures; first cleanup exception retained privately; fixed public uncertainty text. Repeated close does not retry old handles but still drains newly registered handles, avoiding a terminal-success cache incompatibility with unchanged later-adoption paths.
assessment.privacyAndProtocol: Exception objects/tracebacks remain private in-memory state, not durable storage. Proposed protocol covers origin/session, private destination, content/bounds, first-error precedence, commit uncertainty and retention, explicitly unimplemented. No source hash/report/record becomes authority.
assessment.scopePreservation: No bind_leader/worker/diagnostic lifecycle edits, no new import, query/mount/identity checks unchanged. All four launch refusals and legacy source pins unchanged; image inputs/bytes unchanged.
